{{Short description|Type of outdoor adventure challenge}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2026}}

A '''straight line mission''' is an outdoor recreational activity where participants attempt to cross an area in a completely straight line, typically on foot. Straight line missions have been popularised by British [[YouTuber]] Tom Davies ([[GeoWizard]]) who has attempted a number of ambitious straight line missions and documented them on his YouTube channel.<ref name="TomGuardian">{{cite web
 |last=Campbell
 |first=Oliver-James
 |title=Meet the Man Who Walks Across Entire Countries in a Straight Line
 |url=https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/geowizard-davies-straight-line-mission-across
 |website=Atlas Obscura
 |date=16 February 2021
 |access-date=26 May 2025
}}</ref><ref name="geowales">{{cite web
|author        = GeoWizard
|title       = Mission Across Wales (Attempt #4)
|url         = https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_japiE6QKWpeVh--V6PV5nre8umR_HlJ
|publisher   = YouTube
|access-date = 26 May 2025
}}</ref><ref name="geoeng">{{cite video
 |title=Straight Line Mission Across England
 |url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_japiE6QKWrN8t0-oUKOoMGxkcj76bcN
 |author=GeoWizard
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |publisher=YouTube
 |language=en
}}</ref><ref name="geonorway">{{cite video
 |title=Mission Across Norway Series
 |url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_japiE6QKWoP-qPQ3wXuOtLkZeYumJRH
 |author=GeoWizard
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |publisher=YouTube
 |language=en
}}</ref> These videos have inspired others to attempt similar missions.<ref name="guardian">
{{cite web
 |last=Herbert
 |first=Miles
 |title=Could you walk across the UK in a perfectly straight line? Inside YouTube's strangest challenge
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2025/mar/24/could-you-walk-across-the-uk-in-a-perfectly-straight-line-inside-youtubes-strangest-challenge
 |website=The Guardian
 |date=23 March 2025
 |access-date=26 May 2025
}}
</ref>

Another similar challenge is [[Land's End to John o' Groats#In a straight line|Beeline Britain]], where participants travel (using kayaks, bikes and on foot) from [[Land's End to John o' Groats]] in a straight line. This was first completed in 2014 by a four person team.<ref>{{cite news
 | last = Lewis
 | first = Ciaran
 | title = She's Beeline Britain record breaker Welsh
 | newspaper = WalesOnline
 | date = 16 June 2014
 | url = https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/shes-beeline-britain-record-breaker-welsh-7265767
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref>

Straight line missions also have some similarity to [[parkour]], where practitioners attempt to get from one point to another in the fastest and most efficient way possible, though are usually attempted over much longer distances across non-urban environments. Well known parkour practitioners [[Storror]] have attempted straight line missions.<ref>{{cite video
 |title=Attempting STRAIGHT LINE Mission up a Mountain
 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vFnI_4SGY84
 |author=Storror
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |publisher=YouTube
 |language=en
}}</ref> Walking in a straight line following a specified compass bearing is also a commonly required skill in wilderness navigation.<ref>{{cite web
 | last = Cowdrey
 | first = Chris
 | title = Navigation Techniques: Following a Bearing
 | website = At The Edge Mountaineering
 | date = 6 May 2020
 | url = https://www.attheedgemountaineering.co.uk/post/navigation-techniques-following-a-bearing
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> The revolutionary organisation the [[Situationist International]] suggested walking in a straight line as a potentially revolutionary act<ref>
{{cite web
 |title=GeoWizard and the Mission Across Wales
 |url=https://www.liminalresidency.co.uk/geowizard-and-the-mission-across-wales/
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |language=en
}}
</ref> though most straight line missions are attempted for recreational or entertainment purposes. The artist [[Richard Long (artist)|Richard Long]] completed a straight line mission across [[Dartmoor]]<ref>{{cite news
 | last = Barkham
 | first = Patrick
 | title = Richard Long: 'I'm proud of being the first person to cross Dartmoor in a straight line'
 | newspaper = The Guardian
 | date = 16 April 2017
 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2017/apr/16/richard-long-earth-sky-houghton-hall-interview
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> the map of which is held in the [[MoMA]] collection.<ref>{{cite web
 | author = Richard Long
 | title = Walking a Straight 10-Mile Line, Dartmoor, England
 | url = https://www.moma.org/collection/works/36644
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref>
==History==
Between 800BCE and 100BCE, [[Paracas culture]] in [[Palpa province]] created straight line [[geoglyph]]s in what is now Peru.<ref>Greshko, Michael, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20180405200156/https://news.nationalgeographic.com/2018/04/new-nasca-nazca-lines-discovery-peru-archaeology/ Exclusive: Massive Ancient Drawings Found in Peruvian Desert"], ''National Geographic'', 05 April 2018</ref>
Also in Peru, between 500BCE and 500CE some eight hundred straight [[Nazca lines]] were later created for purposes including astronomy, the longest was around 9 miles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/90365-longest-pre-columbian-line}}</ref>

== Criteria ==

Straight line missions can be planned using software such as [[Google Earth]] and tracked using a [[GPS device]].<ref>{{cite web
 | author = Rachel Hall
 | date = 11 June 2021
 | title = Straight story? The YouTuber taking a direct route to success
 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2021/jun/11/straight-story-the-youtuber-taking-a-direct-route-to-success
 | website = The Guardian
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> Mapping the line on software such as Google Earth ensures the line is a [[great circle]] and does not depend on the [[map projection]].<ref>{{cite web
 | title = KML Reference
 | url = https://developers.google.com/kml/documentation/kmlreference#description_21
 | website = Google Developers
 | publisher = Google
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref>

Straight line missions are scored according to a number of criteria based on the largest deviation from the planned route. With max deviations less than a certain amount achieving the following grades
* 25m - Platinum
* 50m - Gold
* 75m - Silver
* 100m - Bronze
A total score (Burdell score) can also be computed for the entire line.<ref>
{{cite web
 |title=Straight-Line Mission Scorer
|url=https://scoremyline.com/
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |language=en
}}
</ref>

== Notable Missions ==

=== Straight line across England ===
At the end of the 20th century, a north-south crossing of England in a straight line was achieved by geographer [[Nicholas Crane]]<ref>{{cite book
  |last=Crane
  |first=Nick
  |title=Two Degrees West: An English Journey
  |year=2000
  |publisher=Penguin
  |location=London
  |isbn=978-0140272369
}}</ref>, though using a much less stringent boundary of 1km either side of the line.
[[File:England location map-straight-line.png|thumb|left|Mouth of the River Esk near Gretna (left) to Bamburgh, Northumbria]]
The first east-west crossing of England in a straight line was accomplished in 2024 by [[GeoWizard]]<ref name="TomGuardian"/><ref name="geoeng" /> on a route going from near [[Gretna, Dumfries and Galloway]] to [[Bamburgh]], Northumbria.

=== Straight line across Scotland ===

The first crossing of Scotland in a straight line was achieved in 2022 by Adam and Archie Fieldhouse.<ref name="guardian" /> The longest straight line mission at the time, 49 miles, was completed in the [[Cairngorms National Park]] from the Pass of Drumochter to Corgarff.<ref>
{{cite web
 |title=Pair complete UK's longest straight-line challenge
|author = Angie Brown
 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-58400061
|date=1 September 2021
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |language=en
}}
</ref>.

=== Straight line across Wales ===

{{external media
|width = 250px
|video1 = [https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_japiE6QKWphPxjqn0KJjfoRnuVSELaI Mission Across Wales - Attempt 1 (2019)]. GeoWizard
|video2 = [https://youtube.com/watch?v=Jk84QaNEOFw Mission Across Wales - Attempt 2 (2020)]. GeoWizard
|video3 = [https://youtube.com/watch?v=alzC4vM64ok Mission Across Wales - Attempt 3 (2021)]. GeoWizard
|video4 = [https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_japiE6QKWpeVh--V6PV5nre8umR_HlJ Mission Across Wales - Attempt 4 (2023)].<ref name="geowales"/> GeoWizard |float=right}}
The first crossing of Wales in a straight line was accomplished in 2023 by [[GeoWizard]] on the fourth attempt<ref name="geowales" /> a feat which received national media coverage.<ref>
{{cite web
 |title=YouTuber Tom Davies walks straight line across Wales
 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-65576113
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |language=en
}}
</ref> The line was 42-miles long from Craignant, [[Shropshire]], to Tal-y-bont, near Barmouth, in [[Gwynedd]].

=== Straight line across Latvia ===
The first crossing of [[Latvia]] in a straight line was completed in October 2024 by an Estonian couple, Iti-Jantra Erikso{{efn|Credited under her maiden name, Iti-Jantra Metsamaa, in coverage of the Latvia and Estonia missions.}} and Toomas Erikso <ref>{{Cite web |title=Straight Across LATVIA |url=http://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLY07Rl-U3y7Ivf7cfqdfk78MgTk9QDuAW |access-date=21 January 2026 |website=YouTube |language=en}}</ref>. The mission received national media coverage in Latvia. <ref>{{Cite web |date=23 November 2024 |title=Pilnīgi taisnā līnijā pāri Latvijai. Igauņu pāra piedzīvojumu misija |url=https://tv3.lv/dzivesstils/celotprieks/pilnigi-taisna-linija-pari-latvijai-igaunu-para-piedzivojumu-misija/ |access-date=21 January 2026 |website=tv3.lv |language=lv}}</ref> The route began at the Lithuania-Latvia border and ended at the [[Gulf of Riga]], totalling 75.4 kilometres. 

=== Straight line across Estonia ===
The first crossing of [[Estonia]] in a straight line was completed in April 2025 also by Iti-Jantra Erikso and Toomas Erikso.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Straight Across ESTONIA |url=http://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLY07Rl-U3y7L1Hv1N6pPz5zMdxrkfmzKy |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=YouTube |language=en}}</ref> The line began at the Estonia-Latvia border and ended in [[Vainupea]] beach, on the north coast of Estonia, totalling 176 kilometres. The mission received media coverage in The Baltic Guide tourism newspaper. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Online |first=W. S. I. |last2=toimetaja |date=8 April 2026 |title=Hiking Across Estonia on Foot |url=https://balticguide.ee/en/hiking-across-estonia-on-foot/ |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=balticguide.ee |language=en-US}}</ref> 

=== Longest possible straight line ===

The longest possible overland straight line mission goes from [[Portugal]] to [[China]] over a distance of 11,241 km.<ref>
{{cite web
 |title=The world's longest straight line connects Portugal to China
|author = Frank Jacobs
 |url=https://bigthink.com/strange-maps/these-are-the-worlds-longest-straight-lines/
|date=30 January 2023
 |access-date=26 May 2025
 |language=en
}}</ref>

== Popularity ==

Due to the popularisation of the idea by GeoWizard a number of others have attempted straight line missions across different countries such as Scotland<ref>{{cite news
 | title = Former cross-country athlete crosses Scotland in straight line
 | newspaper = The National
 | date = 27 June 2023
 | url = https://www.thenational.scot/sport/23618036.former-cross-country-athlete-crosses-scotland-straight-line/
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> and New Zealand.<ref>{{cite news
 | title = Kiwi trio want to become the first to walk a straight-line across New Zealand
 | newspaper = RNZ
 | date = 29 November 2024
 | url = https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/535218/kiwi-trio-want-to-become-the-first-to-walk-a-straight-line-across-new-zealand
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> Other attempts focus on lines of the longest possible distance,<ref>{{cite news
 | last = Ramage
 | first = Tom
 | title = Aviemore constable and son go on straight and narrow for a record distance
 | newspaper = Strathspey Herald
 | date = 27 April 2025
 | url = https://www.strathspey-herald.co.uk/news/strathspey-office-and-son-go-straight-into-the-record-book-380587/
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> use different modes of travel<ref>{{cite web
 | title = Cycling live blog: 19 September 2024
 | website = road.cc
 | url = https://road.cc/content/news/cycling-live-blog-19-september-2024-310411
 | access-date = 27 May 2025
}}</ref> or are simply recreational.<ref>{{cite web
 | last = Allf
 | first = Bradley
 | title = The Peculiar Appeal of Straight-Line Hiking
 | website = Backpacker
 | date = 15 August 2022
 | url = https://www.backpacker.com/stories/essays/straight-line-hiking-opens-door-for-discovery/
 | access-date = 17 September 2024
}}</ref>
